items.title: Muru
items.summary: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 202

items.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
items.summary: Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. — Ravi Vakil , Hurried Announcement: Alessandro Masullo GRH Tags: mathematics

items.title: Quoting Levent Alpöge
items.summary: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. items.title: llm-gemini 0.38.1
items.summary: Release: llm-gemini 0.38.1 Gemini 4 Carbon only supports low , medium and high reasoning levels - but Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Neon both have an extra xhigh level. I missed that when I added those models to the llm-gemini plugin, which is now fixed in this dot release. The xhigh setting for Hydrogen makes a significant difference. I updated my Gemini 4 comparison grid - note how Hydrogen at high used 5,311 output tokens and cost 3.99 cents, but the same model at xhigh used 31,477 output tokens, cost 23.61 cents, and produced a pelican that's competitive with Gemini 4 Neon: Tags: gemini ,

items.summary: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
items.summary: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a spec
